title: Kernel Orchestrator: precision-anchored selection and staged dequant amortization
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: dequantization and mixed-precision handoffs are a major contributor to tail latency and CPU/GPU memory churn for INT8/FP8 serving paths. Existing kernel selection chooses a precision-per-layer heuristic which causes frequent short-lived dequant/req casts during prefill->decode transitions and inflates per-token latency by ~12-18% for real chat workloads.

Goal: implement a Kernel Orchestrator component that selects and anchors execution precision for contiguous spans of work (staged precision anchoring) and amortizes dequant overhead across prefill and subsequent decode steps. The orchestrator should be precision-aware (INT8/FP8/FP16), sequence-length and KV-cache aware, and integrate with the runtime's existing batching and KV shadowing layers. The target is: 1) reduce end-to-end median token latency for mixed-precision models by >=10%, 2) reduce dequant-related CUDA memcpy / kernel launch overhead by >=30% for typical RLHF chat sessions, and 3) keep maximum memory overhead within 5% of current baseline.

Non-goals: exhaustive per-layer per-head autotuning in this ticket (we will add a survey harness separately). This ticket focuses on orchestration, metrics, and a conservative rollout path for production traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator API integrated into runtime kernel selection with a precision anchor concept
Bench harness: microbench showing median token latency reduction >=10% on representative Llama-variant model at batch size 1, seq_len prefills 512 and decode 64
Telemetry: new kernel_selection.precision_anchor and dequant.amortized_bytes metrics reported to telemetry pipeline
E2E smoke: hosted API path passes correctness tests vs FP16 baseline within token-level tolerance (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding distance checks)
Gradual rollout plan documented with canary gates and automatic fallback to per-layer selection
design_summary:
We introduce a short-lived "precision anchor" that pins an execution precision for a logical request segment. Anchors are established at prefill completion and may extend into decode if the expected amortization break-even is met. Anchors are scored using a lightweight estimator: amortized_dequant_cost = estimated_dequant_bytes * device_memcpy_cost + extra_kernel_launches * kernel_launch_cost. Scoring inputs: model dtype support, per-layer dequant factor, KV cache hit probability, remaining decode length, microbatch size, and current GPU occupancy. The orchestrator favors INT8 paths when amortization threshold is positive and falls back to FP16/FP32 otherwise.

Key implementation pieces: orchestrator state machine, kernel adapter layer hooks, small cost model (configurable weights), integration tests, and telemetry. We will implement a feature flag to gate the new orchestrator and an emergency opt-out that reverts to layerwise decisions.

Trade-offs considered: a conservative anchor duration minimizes correctness risk but reduces potential gains for very short decodes. To mitigate, we allow the anchor estimator to consider expected remaining tokens (served estimator from router) and only anchor when expected decode length > 4 tokens or cached KV reuse is high.

Security/compatibility: no changes to model artifacts. The orchestrator only changes serving-time kernel selection. No customer data movement outside current locus.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (prototype): implement orchestrator state machine and cost estimator, add precise hooks into kernel selection path. Unit tests for state transitions. (Assignee: Marco)

Phase 2 (benching): microbench suite for Llama-variant and GPT-style models, measure median and p95 token latencies across batch sizes. Capture dequant memcpy counts and kernel launches. (Assignee: SRE Bench Team)
Phase 3 (canary): feature-flagged rollout to 1% hosted traffic with telemetry and fast rollback. Monitor tail latency and error rate for 48h. (Assignee: Runtime Ops)
Phase 4 (tuning): adjust cost model weights and anchor thresholds based on empirical data, enable broader rollout. (Assignee: Marco + Aisha)
test_plan: Unit tests for orchestrator transitions (anchor open/extend/close)
Integration tests asserting no model output regressions vs FP16 baseline within tolerance
Microbench: synthetic prefill+decode scenarios measuring kernel launch counts and memcpy bytes
Load test at 1% production traffic for 48 hours with automated alerting on latency regressions
A/B evaluation using eval prompts and quality monitors to detect regressions in hallucination or token distribution
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: incorrect anchoring could increase latency for short-lived decodes. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds and opt-out feature flag.
Risk: memory spike due to duplicated dequant buffers. Mitigation: estimator penalizes extra memory; implement a soft cap and LRU dealloc path.
Risk: telemetry blind spots. Mitigation: add explicit metrics for anchor events, amortized_bytes, and fallback_count.
